content.comment_body: Hello, I have a [product_name] connected to a [product_name] HMI panel. I need to change gain and offset parameters from the HMI. Both parameters are included in the VM mapping list from [product_name] programming software and in the TIA tag list. I can only view the value in an I/O field, but can't change it. How can I make these editable? (The I/O field is set to input/output mode.)

The GAIN and OFFSET parameters for an analog amplifier block are only viewable, not writeable. To allow changes via HMI, you would need to implement a custom analog amplifier. This limitation is similar for the [product_name] operator device. See also this related topic: [url]
That's just what I was afraid of. Thanks for the clarification.
Are there other parameters in [product_name] that are also read-only?

Yes, there are many values that can only be read. In [product_name] programming software's HELP section under VM Mapping, you'll find info about which parameters are readable and writable. Indicators like R/W mean you can read and edit, R means read-only and you cannot modify them.
The parameters are included in the attached file.
If I want to change the speed of a motor using the HMI directly from [product_name] to a variable speed drive, what should I do?
Could you specify your goal? Are you trying to change the setpoint of a PI controller, or simply update a value?
A short screen recording is attached. Any block parameter is writable when it displays the icon with a sheet and pencil.
Thank you all. You are awesome. Special thanks to [user_name] for providing the parameter list and their characteristics.

analysis.insight_summary: A key issue highlighted is the inability to edit the gain and offset parameters on the analog amplifier block of [product_name] via HMI, restricting flexibility for users wanting real-time adjustments. The discussion covers which variables are read-only vs writable, but suggests that software feedback and clarity could be improved to help users easily identify editable parameters.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to modify gain and offset parameters of the analog amplifier from the HMI, and to have clear information within [product_name] on which parameters are writable.
